entries.summary: Creates a coordinator whose orders fill at the next bar's open, or at this bar's close when enabled.

parameters.name: broker
parameters.description: A broker with the [`broker.NextOpenBroker`](#broker.NextOpenBroker) methods, normally from [`broker.new`](#broker.new).

parameters.name: portfolio
parameters.description: A portfolio with the [`portfolio.NetLedger`](#portfolio.NetLedger) methods, normally from [`portfolio.new`](#portfolio.new).

entries.returns: A [`trade.NextOpenTrade`](#trade.NextOpenTrade) that owns both values.
entries.body:
Each bar, call `begin_bar(open, bar_index)` before your signal logic and
`end_bar(close, false)` after it. With a broker created with
`processOrdersOnClose = true`, `end_bar` also fills orders at the close,
including orders submitted earlier in the same bar. A broker or portfolio
without the required methods is a compile error.

```tea
import broker
import portfolio
import trade

upper = ta.highest(high, 20)
lower = ta.lowest(low, 20)

var strat = trade.nextOpen(
    broker.new(processOrdersOnClose = true),
    portfolio.new(initialCash = 10000.0)
)
strat.begin_bar(open, bar_index)
if close > upper[1] and strat.position_quantity() == 0.0
    strat.entry("Breakout", trade.Direction.long, sizing = trade.percentOfEquity(50.0))
if close < lower[1] and strat.position_quantity() > 0.0
    strat.close("Breakdown")

strat.end_bar(close, false)
```

exits, then call `end_bar(close, false)`. Use [`trade.path`](#trade.path) instead
when the order of the high and low matters or you need trailing exits.

import portfolio
import trade

entries.summary: Creates a coordinator that replays each bar as an ordered price path, with fixed and trailing exits.

parameters.name: broker
parameters.description: A broker with the [`broker.PathBroker`](#broker.PathBroker) methods, normally from [`broker.new`](#broker.new).

parameters.name: portfolio
parameters.description: A portfolio with the [`portfolio.NetLedger`](#portfolio.NetLedger) methods, normally from [`portfolio.new`](#portfolio.new).

entries.returns: A [`trade.PathTrade`](#trade.PathTrade) that owns both values.
entries.body:
Each bar, call `begin_bar(open, high, low, close, bar_index)`, attach or
adjust exits, call `continue_bar(open, high, low, close)`, submit new
orders, then call `end_bar(close, false)`.

```tea
import broker
import portfolio
import trade

fast = ta.ema(close, 10)
slow = ta.ema(close, 30)
crossedUp = ta.crossover(fast, slow)

var strat = trade.path(broker.new(), portfolio.new(initialCash = 10000.0))
fills = strat.begin_bar(open, high, low, close, bar_index)
if not na(fills.pending) and strat.position_quantity() > 0.0
    // Derive the exit from the entry price; continue_bar checks the rest of this bar.
    entryPrice = strat.position_avg_price()
    strat.exit("Trail", fromEntry = "Long", stop = entryPrice * 0.95, activateOnEntryBar = true, trailPrice = entryPrice * 1.05, trailOffset = entryPrice * 0.02)
strat.continue_bar(open, high, low, close)

    strat.entry("Long", trade.Direction.long, qty = 10.0)

```

entries.summary: Creates a coordinator that opens and closes independently accounted lots immediately, within the current bar.

parameters.name: broker
parameters.description: A broker with the [`broker.ImmediateBroker`](#broker.ImmediateBroker) methods, normally from [`broker.new`](#broker.new).

parameters.name: portfolio
parameters.description: A portfolio with the [`portfolio.LotLedger`](#portfolio.LotLedger) methods, normally from [`portfolio.lots`](#portfolio.lots).

entries.returns: A [`trade.LotTrade`](#trade.LotTrade) that owns both values.
entries.body:
Each bar, call `begin_bar(close, bar_index)`, then `entry`, `close_trade` or
`close_trade_at_stop`, then `mark()`. Each entry fill carries the `tradeId`
that later closes refer to.

```tea
import broker
import portfolio
import trade

basis = ta.sma(close, 20)
crossedUp = ta.crossover(close, basis)
crossedDown = ta.crossunder(close, basis)

var strat = trade.lots(broker.new(), portfolio.lots(initialCash = 10000.0))
var int lotId = 0
var float lotStop = na
strat.begin_bar(close, bar_index)
if lotId > 0
    stopFill = strat.close_trade_at_stop("Stop", lotId, broker.Side.buy, open, high, low, lotStop)
    if not na(stopFill)
        lotId := 0
if lotId > 0 and crossedDown
    strat.close_trade("Exit", lotId)
    lotId := 0
if lotId == 0 and crossedUp
    entryFill = strat.entry("Long", "Cover", trade.Direction.long, notional = 1000.0)
    if not na(entryFill)
        lotId := entryFill.tradeId
        lotStop := close * 0.97
strat.mark()
```

pages.title: broker
pages.description: Order and fill types, and a deterministic broker emulator that fills strategy orders against bar prices.
pages.intro:
Order and fill types, and a deterministic broker emulator that fills strategy orders against bar prices.

A broker turns strategy commands into orders, decides whether, when and at
what price each order fills, applies commission and slippage, and reports
each step as an event. The portfolio library applies fills to cash and
positions, and a trade coordinator sequences broker and portfolio on every
bar. A strategy imports all three, creates a broker with [`broker.new`](#broker.new)
or [`broker.basic`](#broker.basic), and hands it with a portfolio to a coordinator such
as [`trade.nextOpen`](#trade.nextOpen); it then trades through the coordinator rather
than calling the broker. See the strategy model for the full
responsibility boundary and the
backtest guide for a runnable
walkthrough.

The library keeps no global state: each broker value holds its own orders,
ids and matching state. Broker events are appended to one output per event
type, such as `broker.FillExecuted`; each output keeps execution order, but
separate outputs share no ordering.

```tea
import broker
import portfolio
import trade

fast = ta.ema(close, 10)
slow = ta.ema(close, 30)

var strat = trade.nextOpen(
    broker.new(commission = broker.commissionRate(0.001)),
    portfolio.new(initialCash = 10000.0)
)

strat.begin_bar(open, bar_index)
if ta.crossover(fast, slow)
    strat.entry("Long", trade.Direction.long)
if ta.crossunder(fast, slow)
    strat.close("Long")
strat.end_bar(close, false)

metrics = strat.snapshot()
plot("equity", metrics.equity, "equity")
```

Add `import broker` to a script to use these as `broker.name`.

With the defaults it charges no commission or slippage. With
`processOrdersOnClose = true`, the next-open and OHLC coordinators also fill
pending commands at bar closes, including the close of the bar a command was
issued on. Pass the result to a trade coordinator such as
[`trade.nextOpen`](#trade.nextOpen).

```tea
import broker
import portfolio
import trade

var strat = trade.ohlc(
    broker.new(
        commission = broker.commissionPercent(0.05),
        slippage = broker.slippageTicks(1.0, 0.01),
        processOrdersOnClose = true
    ),
    portfolio.new(initialCash = 10000.0)
)

average = ta.sma(close, 20)
strat.begin_bar(open, high, low, bar_index)
if ta.crossover(close, average)
    // Fills at this bar's close because processOrdersOnClose is true.
    strat.entry("Long", trade.Direction.long, qty = 10.0)
strat.end_bar(close, false)
```

entries.body:
It keeps a deliberately small order model: one pending command (a market or
stop entry, a close, or a rebalance) and one attached exit (stop, target,
bracket or trailing stop). It is not a general order book, and a target is
not a true limit order: adverse slippage still applies after it matches. The
scheduled methods make at most two fills per bar; an order beyond that
waits, and a reversal's opening fill moves to the next open.

All of its state lives in its fields, so a script can run several
independent brokers. The trade coordinators call its methods in a fixed
order on every bar, and strategies use the coordinator instead. The
strategy model describes each coordinator's matching rules.

must be below `1`, and tick slippage needs a tick size that is not `na`

entries.returns: the accepted order, or `na` when rejected.
entries.body:
An entry with a `stop` becomes a stop order and anything else a market
order. A pending stop entry is replaced by a stop entry with the same
id, and a pending rebalance by a rebalance with the same id; the old
order is cancelled. Invalid commands, and commands that would need a
second pending order, are rejected; see [`broker.Rejection`](#broker.Rejection). Called
by the coordinators' `entry`, `close` and `rebalance`.

`trailOffset`), all positive, with a long exit's stop below its target
and a short exit's above. It replaces an attached exit only when both
the command id and the entry match. Called by `exit` of
[`trade.OhlcTrade`](#trade.OhlcTrade) and [`trade.PathTrade`](#trade.PathTrade).

position is open. Called by the coordinators' `cancel`.

    broker.Command command,
    float closePrice,
    broker.Account account,
    int barIndex
)

parameters.name: closePrice
parameters.description: the bar's close, used as the reference price

entries.returns: the fill, or `na` when rejected.
entries.body:
The command needs exactly one positive `quantity` or `notional`. An
entry needs pyramiding capacity and, unless its margin is `0`, enough
capital, and gets a new stable trade id; a close needs a positive
`tradeId` and the side opposite the open position. Emits
[`broker.OrderSubmitted`](#broker.OrderSubmitted) and [`broker.FillExecuted`](#broker.FillExecuted) on
success. Called by `entry` and `close_trade` of [`trade.LotTrade`](#trade.LotTrade).

signatures:
broker.Fill execute(
    float referencePrice,
    broker.Account account,
    int barIndex,
    bool atClose,
    bool priceTriggered = true,
    bool reversalContinuation = false
)

parameters.name: priceTriggered
parameters.description: whether the caller's trigger check passed

parameters.name: reversalContinuation
parameters.description: whether this call completes a reversal

entries.returns: the fill, or `na`.
entries.body:
A command is eligible on any bar after its signal bar, or from its
signal bar on during close processing with `processOrdersOnClose` set,
and only while the bar has fewer than two fills. Once attempted, it
stops being pending whether it filled or was rejected, unless a reversal
still owes its opening fill.

entries.summary: Matches the pending command at the bar's open.
signatures:
broker.Fill on_open(
    float referencePrice,
    broker.Account account,
    int barIndex
)
entries.returns: the fill, or `na`.
entries.body:
Market orders fill at the open, and a stop entry fills there when the
open is at or past its stop; a reversal deferred from an earlier bar
completes here. Commands issued on this bar wait for a later bar. Called
by `begin_bar` of [`trade.NextOpenTrade`](#trade.NextOpenTrade).

entries.summary: Matches the pending command against the bar's open, high and low.
signatures:
broker.Fill match_pending(
    float openPrice,
    float highPrice,
    float lowPrice,
    broker.Account account,
    int barIndex
)
entries.returns: the fill, or `na`.
entries.body:
Market orders fill at the open. A stop entry fills at the open when the
bar gaps past its stop, otherwise at the stop when the high (buy) or low
(sell) reaches it. A reversal deferred from an earlier bar completes at
the open. Called by `begin_bar` of [`trade.OhlcTrade`](#trade.OhlcTrade).

entries.summary: Matches the pending command along the bar's path `open -> nearer extreme -> farther extreme -> close`.
signatures:
broker.Fill match_path_primary(
    float openPrice,
    float highPrice,
    float lowPrice,
    float closePrice,
    broker.Account account,
    int barIndex
)
entries.returns: the fill, or `na`.
entries.body:
The extreme nearer the open comes first, and the low on a tie. Market
orders fill at the open; a stop entry fills at the open on a gap,
otherwise at its stop on the first segment that reaches it. The fill's
place on the path is recorded so `match_path_exit` continues from there.
Called by `begin_bar` of [`trade.PathTrade`](#trade.PathTrade).

entries.summary: Completes a reversal's opening fill on the same bar, at the closing fill's reference price.
signatures:
broker.Fill continue_reversal(
    broker.Account account,
    int barIndex
)

parameters.name: account
parameters.description: account view refreshed after the closing fill

entries.returns: the opening fill, or `na`.
entries.body:
The coordinators call it right after the portfolio applies the first
fill, so sizing sees the refreshed account. It does nothing without a
pending reversal, or when the bar already has two fills; the reversal
then completes at the next open.

entries.summary: Matches the attached exit against the bar's open, high and low, closing the whole position.
signatures:
broker.Fill match_exit(
    float openPrice,
    float highPrice,
    float lowPrice,
    broker.Account account,
    int barIndex
)
entries.returns: the exit fill, or `na`.
entries.body:
The exit is live while its entry holds the position, from the bar after
the entry fill unless `activateOnEntryBar` is set. A gap past the stop
or target fills at the open; otherwise a touched level fills at that
level, and when both are touched, the side whose extreme is nearer the
open wins, ties going to the stop. A triggered exit is removed even if
its fill is rejected, and outside `match_path_exit` a trailing exit is
rejected and removed. Tick slippage cannot take the exit price below one
tick. Called by `begin_bar` of [`trade.OhlcTrade`](#trade.OhlcTrade).

entries.summary: Activates and ratchets the trailing stop over one path segment.
signatures:
int update_trail(
    float fromPrice,
    float toPrice,
    broker.Account account,
    int barIndex
)
entries.body:
It activates once price reaches `trailPrice`, then keeps the stop
`trailOffset` behind the best price so far; only moves in the position's
favor advance it.

entries.summary: Matches the attached exit on one path segment, then updates the trailing stop if nothing filled.
signatures:
broker.Fill match_path_exit_segment(
    float fromPrice,
    float toPrice,
    broker.Account account,
    int barIndex
)
entries.returns: the exit fill, or `na`.
entries.body: A trailing stop moved by a segment applies from the next segment.

entries.summary: Matches the attached exit along the rest of the bar's path, segment by segment.
signatures:
broker.Fill match_path_exit(
    float openPrice,
    float highPrice,
    float lowPrice,
    float closePrice,
    broker.Account account,
    int barIndex
)
entries.returns: the exit fill, or `na`.
entries.body:
It starts where the pending command filled on this bar, or at the open,
so earlier prices on the bar cannot trigger the exit; trailing stops
activate and ratchet as the path advances. Called by `continue_bar` of
[`trade.PathTrade`](#trade.PathTrade).

entries.summary: Matches the pending command at the bar's close when `processOrdersOnClose` is set.
signatures:
broker.Fill on_close(
    float referencePrice,
    broker.Account account,
    int barIndex
)
entries.returns: the fill, or `na`.
entries.body:
Commands issued on this bar are eligible. Market orders fill at the
close, and a stop entry fills when the close is at or past its stop.
Called by `end_bar` and `process_close` of [`trade.NextOpenTrade`](#trade.NextOpenTrade)
and [`trade.OhlcTrade`](#trade.OhlcTrade).

entries.summary: Expires the pending command and the attached exit, and clears entry, reversal and trailing state.
entries.returns: the expired orders.
entries.body:
Emits [`broker.OrderExpired`](#broker.OrderExpired) for each expired order; it does not
close positions. Called by the coordinators' `end_bar` and `finish` on
the final bar.

pages.description: Portfolios that account for a strategy's fills: cash, positions, fees, profit and drawdown.
pages.intro:
Portfolios that account for a strategy's fills: cash, positions, fees, profit and drawdown.

Add `import portfolio` together with `import broker` and `import trade`.
Create a portfolio with [`portfolio.new`](#portfolio.new) for one net position, or with
[`portfolio.lots`](#portfolio.lots) for separately tracked lots, and pass it to a
coordinator from the `trade` library, which applies every [`broker.Fill`](#broker.Fill)
the broker returns. A portfolio never decides whether, when or at what price
an order fills. Read results through the coordinator's `snapshot()`.

The interfaces list what each coordinator needs from a portfolio. A type
satisfies one when it has every listed method with the same parameter
types, result type and `const` marking; parameter names do not matter.

```tea
import broker
import portfolio
import trade

trend = ta.sma(close, 50)
crossedUp = ta.crossover(close, trend)
crossedDown = ta.crossunder(close, trend)

var strat = trade.nextOpen(
    broker.new(commission = broker.commissionRate(0.001)),
    portfolio.new(initialCash = 50000.0)
)
strat.begin_bar(open, bar_index)
if crossedUp and strat.position_quantity() == 0.0
    strat.entry("Trend", trade.Direction.long, sizing = trade.percentOfEquity(40.0))
if crossedDown and strat.position_quantity() > 0.0
    strat.close("Exit")
strat.end_bar(close, false)

metrics = strat.snapshot()
plot("equity", metrics.equity)
plot("max drawdown", metrics.maxDrawdown)
plot("win rate", metrics.winRate)
```

Add `import portfolio` to a script to use these as `portfolio.name`.

pages.description: Orientation and contact tests for line segments, quadratic curves and rectangles.
pages.intro:
Orientation and contact tests for line segments, quadratic curves and rectangles.

Each point is a pair of `x` and `y` numbers on a plane with `y` pointing up.
The library gives coordinates no time, price or pixel meaning, so choose the
mapping yourself, for example `bar_index` as `x` and a price as `y`. Every
function rejects a coordinate that [`geometry.coordinateSupported`](#geometry.coordinateSupported)
rejects, including `na`: [`geometry.orient2d`](#geometry.orient2d) then returns `na`,
[`geometry.segmentContact`](#geometry.segmentContact) returns `false`, and the functions that
return arrays return an empty one.

[`geometry.orient2d`](#geometry.orient2d) and [`geometry.segmentContact`](#geometry.segmentContact) are exact for
Float64 arithmetic on the CPU, a guarantee that does not extend to GPU
execution. Positions along the shapes, and the contacts of quadratic curves,
are computed in Float64 within small rounding bounds. See
geometry for the algorithms and numerical limits.

Add `import geometry` to a script to use these as `geometry.name`.

entries.summary: Tells whether a number can be used as a coordinate by this library.
entries.returns: `true` when `value` is a supported coordinate, otherwise `false`.
entries.body:
Accepts `0` and finite numbers whose magnitude is from `1e-70` through
`1e70`, and rejects `na` and everything else; the range keeps the exact
arithmetic free of overflow and underflow. Check inputs with it to skip
evaluation when data is missing, such as `close[1]` on the first row.

entries.summary: Tells whether three points turn clockwise, turn counterclockwise or lie on one line.
signatures:
geometry.orient2d(
    float ax,
    float ay,
    float bx,
    float by,
    float cx,
    float cy
)
entries.returns: A positive number, a negative number or `0`; `na` when a coordinate is unsupported.
entries.body:
The result is positive when `a`, `b`, `c` turn clockwise, so `c` lies to the
right of the line from `a` through `b`; negative when they turn
counterclockwise; and `0` when the points are collinear. The sign is exact,
but the magnitude is not a reliable area, so use only the sign.

entries.summary: Tests whether two line segments share at least one point.
signatures:
geometry.segmentContact(
    float ax,
    float ay,
    float bx,
    float by,
    float px,
    float py,
    float qx,
    float qy
)
entries.returns: `true` when the segments touch; `false` when they do not or a coordinate is unsupported.
entries.body:
Both segments include their endpoints, so touching at an end counts, as does
overlapping along one line; a segment whose ends are equal is a single point.
The decision is exact. This tests whether the move from the previous close to
the current one touches a line from `(0, 100)` to `(100, 110)`, with
`bar_index` as `x`; on the first row `close[1]` is `na`, so the result is
`false`:

```tea
import geometry

hit = geometry.segmentContact(0.0, 100.0, 100.0, 110.0, bar_index - 1, close[1], bar_index, close)
emit "hit" hit
```

entries.summary: Finds where an observation segment meets a line segment, with the position on each.
signatures:
geometry.segmentContacts(
    float ax,
    float ay,
    float bx,
    float by,
    float px,
    float py,
    float qx,
    float qy
)
entries.returns: An array of up to two [`geometry.Contact`](#geometry.Contact) values; empty when the segments do not touch or a coordinate is unsupported.
entries.body:
The segment from `a` to `b` is the primitive and the segment from `p` to `q`
is the observation. A crossing or a single shared point gives one
[`geometry.Contact`](#geometry.Contact). Segments that overlap along one line give two,
marking the ends of the shared stretch, with `overlap` set to `true` and
`boundaryParameter` set to `na`. Whether the segments touch is decided
exactly, as in [`geometry.segmentContact`](#geometry.segmentContact); the positions are then
computed in Float64. Each call returns a new array, and the order of its
contacts is not defined.

entries.summary: Finds where an observation segment meets a quadratic Bézier curve, with the position on each.
signatures:
geometry.quadraticContacts(
    float ax,
    float ay,
    float bx,
    float by,
    float cx,
    float cy,
    float px,
    float py,
    float qx,
    float qy
)
entries.returns: An array of up to two [`geometry.Contact`](#geometry.Contact) values; empty when the shapes do not touch or a coordinate is unsupported.
entries.body:
The curve starts at `a`, bends toward the control point `b` and ends at `c`;
the observation runs from `p` to `q`. Each crossing or tangent touch gives
one [`geometry.Contact`](#geometry.Contact), and its `transverse` field tells the two apart.
When the whole curve lies along the observation's line, the contacts instead
mark the ends of the shared stretch, or its single point, with
`boundaryParameter` set to `na`: a curve can double back along the line, so
a point there has no unique position on the curve. Contacts come from
Float64 root finding, accepted within a rounding allowance of 32 machine
epsilons rather than any price or pixel distance. Each call returns a new
array, and the order of its contacts is not defined.

entries.summary: Tests whether a segment or quadratic curve touches a closed rectangle, returning one shared point.
signatures:
geometry.rectangleContacts(
    float ax,
    float ay,
    float bx,
    float by,
    float cx,
    float cy,
    bool quadratic,
    float left,
    float bottom,
    float right,
    float top
)

parameters.name: bx
parameters.description: `x` of the control point, `b`. Ignored when `quadratic` is `false`, but it must still be a supported coordinate.

parameters.name: by
parameters.description: `y` of `b`, with the same rule as `bx`.

parameters.name: quadratic
parameters.description: `true` for the quadratic curve with control point `b`, `false` for the segment from `a` to `c`.

entries.returns: An array holding one [`geometry.Point`](#geometry.Point) where the shapes meet; empty when they do not, when `left` is greater than `right` or `bottom` greater than `top`, or when a coordinate is unsupported.
entries.body:
The rectangle includes its interior, so a shape wholly inside it touches it.
With `quadratic` set to `false` the shape is the segment from `a` to `c`;
otherwise it is the quadratic curve from `a` toward the control point `b` to
`c`. The result holds at most one point: where the shape meets an edge, or a
contained endpoint when the shape lies wholly inside. That point proves
contact; it is not necessarily the first contact along the shape. A
rectangle of zero width or height is allowed.

entries.summary: One place where an observation segment meets a segment or curve.

rows:
Position on the primitive, from `0` at its start to `1` at its end. `na` at either end of an overlap, and for every contact of a quadratic
curve that lies along the observation's line.
Position on the observation, from `0` at `p` to `1` at `q`. `0` when the observation is a single point.

Whether the observation meets the primitive at an angle rather than along or tangent to it. `true` even at an endpoint; `false` for a tangent touch, a point
observation and shapes on one line. It does not tell whether a path passes
to the other side.
Whether the contact is one end of a stretch where the two shapes overlap.

entries.body:
[`geometry.segmentContacts`](#geometry.segmentContacts) and [`geometry.quadraticContacts`](#geometry.quadraticContacts)
return these. The segment or curve passed first is the primitive, and the
segment from `p` to `q` is the observation. Positions on a shape run from `0`
at its start to `1` at its end; on a quadratic curve the position is the
curve parameter, which is not proportional to length.

entries.summary: A point on the plane, as returned by [`geometry.rectangleContacts`](#geometry.rectangleContacts).
